comparator.name: History
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 History EER and student curriculum describe the 180 EC full-time English-taught BA. The History track and Foundations of Europe are selected by official order. The major includes 60 EC of foundational courses, a 30 EC depth package, 15 EC of track-specific writing and historical foundations, and a 15 EC thesis. Research Seminar A, Writing Skills for Historians and Theory of History require 45 EC at introductory level. The 2026 cohort student curriculum and regulations control over the public recruitment overview where the Year 2 structures differ. Thesis entry requires 30 EC at advanced level and a qualifying Seminar A. The 60 EC profiling space includes a 30 EC coherent package and 30 EC of free electives. At least 15 EC of the profiling space must be at level 2 or 3.

components.name: Bachelor’s Thesis in History (GE3V23002)
components.note: Students must earn at least 30 EC at advanced level and complete a qualifying Research Seminar A before starting the 15 EC thesis.

components.name: Coherent elective package
components.note: Choose a minor or approved study abroad. Across the full 60 EC of electives, at least 15 EC must be at level 2 or 3.

components.name: Open electives
components.note: Options include individual courses, a second minor or an internship of up to 15 EC.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized History target does not select between the two formal tracks or among their seven specialisations. The adopted 2026-2027 EER lists Track History before International Relations in Historical Perspective and lists The Foundations of Europe first within Track History. That package is therefore selected by official order, before and independently of UCR course selection. The 60-EC optional course profile remains open because the EER does not prescribe one subject.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest option links chronological and cultural history with archaeology, art and research methods. The international relations and conflict option owns the historical study of global power and conflict. The inequality and political economy option owns historical inequality and economic change. Each has a distinct academic focus, and all three retain the shared six-course history spine. Careers and individual examples do not generate additional options.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: UCR Modern History covers modernity, imperialism, war and decolonisation. Utrecht provides a dedicated contemporary history survey.
UCR History of Empires studies power, legitimacy and identity across empires. Utrecht concentrates on the foundations of Europe and the role of religion.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Research Seminar B: Foundations of Europe (GE3V21015).
UCR Introduction to World Archaeology uses material sources to interpret ancient societies across regions. Utrecht approaches the ancient world through historical study.
UCR studies Renaissance Italy and Mediterranean exchange through art and material culture. Utrecht surveys a broader span of early modern and modern history.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Cities and Citizens (GE3V20003).
Both develop research questions, evaluate historical sources and write an argument. UCR’s course studies the American Century, while Utrecht’s seminar is part of the Foundations of Europe package.
UCR has no scheduled course providing the dedicated medieval-history breadth and weight of Utrecht's compulsory course.
UCR introduces statistical analysis and research design. Utrecht applies data to historical questions.
Both develop systematic inquiry and source interpretation. UCR studies qualitative social research, while Utrecht teaches historical research.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Writing Skills for Historians (GE2V17008).
UCR examines how scholars interpret and write the history of art. Utrecht introduces history as a wider discipline.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Bachelor’s Thesis in History (GE3V23002).
No second scheduled UCR course reproduces Utrecht's full compulsory historical-research-laboratory sequence.
UCR courses provide philosophical and social context, but no scheduled course is a dedicated foundations-of-history requirement at Utrecht's specified scope.
Utrecht's 30-EC minor or approved study-abroad package is genuine open profiling space; no single content is invented or equated to one UCR course.

Utrecht's remaining 30 EC is genuine free space, potentially including an internship; UCR choice is distributed across the liberal-arts curriculum and no one scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.
